biggest_catch: $0 annual fee, so the 10,000 TrueBlue points are pure upside on the fee side — but this is the basic JetBlue Card, distinct from the JetBlue Plus card, and the points only help if you fly JetBlue. Only net purchases count toward the $1,000-in-90-days, so spend only what you already planned — never overspend to chase the bonus. Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, and carrying a balance at the card's ~20%+ variable APR erases the points fast — pay in full every month.
catches: Only pursue spending you already planned to do — never buy extra things just to hit a bonus threshold; overspending to chase a bonus wipes out the bonus math and is how people lose money on it.
This is the basic JetBlue Card (10,000 points), not the JetBlue Plus Card — different bonus, different product.
Only net purchases count toward the $1,000; returns and cash-like transactions do not.
Current or previous TrueBlue program-account holders may be ineligible for the bonus.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily dip your credit score by a few points.
The card's variable APR (~20%+) will erase the points' value fast if you carry a balance — pay the full statement balance every month.
